question: An object moves 10 m in 2 s. On a distance–time graph, what is the slope?
solution:
The correct answer is __**5 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **slope** of a **distance-time graph** represents the **speed** of an object. In physics, the slope is defined as the vertical change (rise) divided by the horizontal change (run).
 
• For a distance-time graph, the **distance** is plotted on the **Y-axis** (vertical) and **time** is plotted on the **X-axis** (horizontal).
 
• In the given problem, the **total distance** moved by the object is **10 m** and the **time interval** is **2 s**.
 
• The formula to calculate the **slope** is: **Slope = Change in Distance / Change in Time**.
 
• By substituting the values, we get: **Slope = 10 m / 2 s = 5 m/s**. ***Hence, the calculated value is 5 m/s.***
 
• This result tells us that the object is traveling at a **constant speed** of **5 meters per second** if the graph is a straight line.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Speed vs. Velocity:** 
 
 
• **Speed** is a **scalar quantity** that refers to "how fast an object is moving." It only has **magnitude** and is calculated as **distance divided by time**.
 
• **Velocity** is a **vector quantity** that refers to "the rate at which an object changes its position." It requires both **magnitude** and **direction** and is calculated as **displacement divided by time**.
 
 
 
• **SI Units:** The **International System of Units (SI)** unit for speed is **meters per second (m/s)**. Other commonly used units include **kilometers per hour (km/h)** and **miles per hour (mph)**.
 
• **Types of Motion on a Graph:**
 
 
• A **straight line** with a positive slope indicates **uniform motion**, meaning the object moves at a **constant speed**.
 
• A **curved line** indicates **non-uniform motion** or **acceleration**, where the speed of the object is changing over time.
 
• A **horizontal line** (parallel to the time axis) indicates that the **slope is zero**, meaning the object is at **rest** (speed is **0 m/s**).
 
 
 
• **Steepness:** The **steeper** the slope of the line on a distance-time graph, the **higher** the speed of the object. A line closer to the time axis represents a slower speed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Graphical Interpretation:** To find the **instantaneous speed** at any point on a non-linear distance-time graph, one must draw a **tangent** to the curve at that specific point and calculate its slope.
 
• **Negative Slope:** On a **displacement-time graph**, a **negative slope** indicates that the object is moving back toward the **starting position**. However, on a **distance-time graph**, the slope cannot be negative because total distance covered never decreases with time.
 
• **Comparison:** If two lines are drawn on the same graph, the one with the higher **gradient** represents the object with the greater speed. For example, a line with a slope of **10 m/s** is steeper than the one calculated in this question (**5 m/s**).
 
• **Conversion:** To convert speed from **m/s** to **km/h**, multiply the value by **3.6** (or **18/5**). Therefore, **5 m/s** is equivalent to **18 km/h**.
